entries.title: The quiz keeps your answers and their marks
entries.body: When you come back to a quiz question after reloading the page, switching mode, or moving on and back, your answer and its mark are there. If an answer cannot be saved, or your earlier answers cannot be loaded, the quiz says so. Your answers are included when you export your data, and the privacy page has been updated to say they are stored. Whether an answer was right or wrong is still not kept.

entries.title: Timeline shows the article's words for yearless dates
entries.body: Where Timeline could not tell a date's year, it showed "dated — but which year?". It shows the date as the article wrote it instead, and the heading says which years were assumed. When a timeline is rebuilt for an article with no usable publication date, a year the article itself states can sometimes fill the gap, marked "(year assumed)".

entries.title: The reading-time estimate explains itself
entries.body: Point at the reading time at the top of an article, or at Read time on its Metadata page, and a card shows the word count, the rate used and the limits of the estimate. The rate is a flat 238 words a minute whatever the piece, and the card says so. Both can be reached from the keyboard.

entries.title: Switch dark and light from the command bar
entries.body: If you are signed in, type "dark mode", "light mode" or "theme" in the command bar to set the appearance to Dark, Light or System, without going to your profile page. The one in use is marked as current.

entries.title: End mark for articles, dates on library cards
entries.body: A small mark sits under the last paragraph of an article, so you can tell the piece has ended rather than stopped loading. In your library, each article's card shows its publication date after the author and site, where the article has one.

entries.title: Clicking a Structure row marks the right row
entries.body: After you clicked a row in Structure on a long article, the article went to the right place, but the address then changed to the section before, and the row before the one you clicked was highlighted. Both follow your click. The controls bar also stays in view after a jump further down the page.

entries.title: Long uploaded PDFs get their source looked up
entries.body: When you open a PDF you uploaded, the app tries to identify where it comes from. For longer PDFs that lookup failed without searching at all; it runs as it does for shorter ones. A lookup that already finished without success is not tried again automatically.

entries.title: Fewer problems in tabs left open across updates
entries.body: In a tab left open while the app was updated, opening an article's Metadata page could bring up the error screen; the page opens instead. The changelog page checks for a newer version and reloads itself, but not when that would lose a draft, an upload or unsaved text, and never more than once for the same version.
